entries.title: US, South Korea and Japan Renew Commitment to North Korea’s Denuclearization
entries.paragraph_1: The United States, South Korea and Japan have renewed their commitment to the “complete denuclearization” of North Korea as Pyongyang continues to reject disarmament ahead of possible nuclear talks with Washington. Speculation has grown over a possible meeting between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during next month’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China, following repeated overtures by Trump for renewed nuclear negotiations. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi reaffirmed their position during a meeting on Friday on the sidelines of the Group of 20 (G20) gathering in Atlanta, Georgia. Advertisement According to the US State Department, the three officials “reaffirmed their resolute commitment to the complete denuclearization” of North Korea. They also pledged to ensure the “full implementation” of United Nations Security Council resolutions, including measures prohibiting support for revenue-generating activities linked to North Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes. Despite years of international sanctions, North Korea, which enjoys support from Russia and China, has legally entrenched its status as a nuclear-armed state. Its government has repeatedly insisted that its nuclear arsenal is permanent and irreversible. Advertisement Trump open to meeting Kim Trump has repeatedly expressed willingness to engage Pyongyang in nuclear negotiations while reducing joint military exercises with South Korea, a key US ally. The US president departed from longstanding American policy last year when he acknowledged that North Korea was already “sort of a nuclear power”. He also signalled that he was “100 percent” open to meeting Kim, although the North Korean leader did not respond to the proposal. Advertisement Analysts and South Korea’s intelligence agency believe Kim may have communicated Pyongyang’s position on possible talks with Trump to Beijing during a recent visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong. South Korea’s President Lee Jae Myung, who has adopted a more conciliatory approach towards Pyongyang, has repeatedly called for dialogue without preconditions. In September, Lee suggested that Washington consider pursuing a freeze on North Korea’s nuclear programme rather than demanding its immediate dismantlement, in exchange for sanctions relief. Advertisement However, critics argue that such a proposal could amount to tacit recognition of North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to secure sanctions relief without surrendering its weapons. Some analysts also believe China may be moving towards accepting North Korea’s nuclear status, citing the absence of references to denuclearisation in statements issued after Kim met Chinese President Xi Jinping in June. Meanwhile, Pyongyang on Saturday criticised a joint statement issued by a group of countries monitoring the implementation of sanctions against it. Advertisement North Korea insisted that “the stereotyped sanctions racket of the US and the West can neither influence the position of the DPRK (North Korea) as a nuclear weapons state”. entries.paragraph_1: 포스코 노사가 기본급 2.6% 인상을 중심으로 한 2026년 임금 협약에 잠정 합의했다. 지난 6월 16일 임금 교섭을 시작한 지 약 4개월여 만이다. 양측은 30일 오전 10시 30분부터 경북 포항 본사에서 만나 임금 협상과 관련해 본교섭을 진행해 이날 오후 늦게 잠정 합의안을 도출했다. 잠정 합의안은 기본급 2.6% 인상, 일시금 600만원, 특별승호 3호봉, 명절 상여금 200만원+기본급 20%(2028년 이후 30%로 상향), 교대휴일수당추가, 상주·정비수당 2만원, 의료제도개선(배우자, 자녀 추가) 등을 담았다. 한국노총 금속노련 포스코노동조합은 잠정 합의안을 바탕으로 조만간 조합원 찬반투표를 통해 잠정안 추인에 나선다. 조합원 과반수가 찬성하면 임금 협약은 타결된다. 앞서 포스코 노조는 지난 6월 16일 회사 측과 임금 교섭을 시작해 그동안 약 30차례에 걸쳐 실무·본교섭을 진행했으나 의견 차이로 합의에 이르지 못했다. 전소연 기자 soyeon@etnews.com

entries.title: North Korea answers South’s proposal for military talks by firing off ballistic missiles
entries.paragraph_1: North Korea fired more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward the East Sea on Thursday, 17 days after its previous ballistic missile launch on Oct. 12. South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected the projectile launches from the Wonsan area around 12:30 pm. The launches came six days after South Korea’s Ministry of National Defense proposed military talks with North Korea on Oct. 23 to prevent accidental clashes along the Military Demarcation Line following recent land mine explosions in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ). According to the Joint Chiefs, the missiles traveled around 250 kilometers. South Korean and US authorities are currently analyzing the technical details. The missiles were reportedly among a range of weapons systems — including 600 mm super-large multiple rocket launchers — that North Korean forces drilled on Thursday. South Korea’s National Security Office convened an emergency meeting with officials from the Defense Ministry, the Joint Chiefs and other relevant agencies to review the security situation. “We emphasized the need to thoroughly assess the implications of the launches for our security and ensure that all necessary measures are taken,” an office spokesperson said after the meeting. The office also urged North Korea to immediately halt its repeated ballistic missile launches, calling them “violations of UN Security Council resolutions and grave actions that do nothing to help contain the current situation.”
entries.paragraph_2: By Jang Na-rye, staff reporter; Kwon Hyuk-chul, staff reporter

entries.title: AI chip smugglers exploit trade control loophole to bring banned HBM from South Korea into China — expensive memory chips packaged with cheap, unsanctioned processors to become legal exports | Tom's Hardware
entries.paragraph_1: A memory smuggler has detailed how he gets export-controlled HBM chips from South Korea into China using a loophole. According to The Information , the smuggler owns a chip design firm that build cheap, low-performing processors that fall under the U.S. and South Korea’s export controls. They are then paired with expensive HBM from Samsung and SK hynix, that, on their own, are banned for export to China. But because export control rules only look at the performance of the server processor and not at the other components attached to it, this allows the HBM chips attached inside them to slip under the radar and make their way into China.
entries.paragraph_2: It’s not a risk-free operation, though. Once the mediocre processors with high-end memory chips land in Hong Kong and are smuggled across the border into Shenzhen in the luggage of commuters that cross between the two regions daily, they end up in workshops where technicians heat up the boards to soften the solder, gingerly lift the crucial memory chips, and discard the rest of the components. Despite having a high failure rate, the high price of HBM chips makes the procedure quite lucrative.

entries.title: South Korea Chip Exports Approach Half of Economy; First Trillion-Dollar Year Due in November
entries.paragraph_1: South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy released October 2026 export data Sunday to figures that would have been implausible at any prior point in the country's industrial history: semiconductor shipments reached $56.4 billion for the month, an increase of 259.4% from October 2025, and accounted for 48.9% of all South Korean goods exported — making chips nearly one dollar out of every two that left the country. Total exports across all categories hit $115.3 billion, a 93.7% year-on-year gain and the highest October figure in the country's history, extending a streak of monthly records that has turned 2026 into the most extraordinary year for Korean trade in modern memory.
entries.paragraph_2: The driver is structural, not cyclical. South Korea produces an estimated 80–90% of the world's High Bandwidth Memory — the specialized, stacked-DRAM architecture that AI accelerators require to perform inference at scale — and demand for that memory has grown in direct proportion to the global AI infrastructure buildout. As hyperscalers spend hundreds of billions of dollars expanding AI data center capacity, every GPU they deploy must be paired with HBM that, with very few exceptions, can only come from South Korea.
